Watch: new Jira tickets matching this JQL:
project = "ES"

Each run:
1. Read your state from your most recent reply in this session that has a "Checked through:" line: that check time, and any "Delivery pending:" and "Link-back pending:" lines. On the first run, use one hour ago and nothing pending. If you have no way to use Jira here, or signing in to it fails, skip to your reply and say that this automation needs a Jira MCP server where it runs.
2. For each pending delivery, find its session: by its conversation_id, or, for an unconfirmed start listed without one, by its title among the sessions you created (sys_session_list with include_archived true, following next_cursor through every page). If no such session exists and the listed rows carry an archived field (so archived sessions were included), the start never happened: drop the entry, fetch that ticket again by the key in its title, and handle it with this run's matches below, since the search window may have moved past it. If the rows have no archived field, an archived session could be hiding: keep the entry pending and ask the owner in your reply to check for that session. Otherwise read that session's history with sys_session_get_history. If your task message is there, it was delivered: drop the entry. If it isn't, keep the entry pending and point the owner to that session in your reply: the task may still be queued where the history can't show it, so never resend it and never create another session for it.
3. Post each pending link-back, the same way as below. Don't start sessions for them; one that fails again stays pending.
4. Note the current UTC time; it ends this run's window. Then search from 5 minutes before the check time, because new items can take a few minutes to appear. Use your Jira tools to search for (project = "ES") AND created >= <that time> ORDER BY created ASC. A relative time such as "-90m" avoids time zone mistakes. Leave out results created after the time you noted; the next run picks them up. Read every page of results in that order. If you can't read them all, stop at the last result you read.

For results not listed there, call sys_session_list once with include_archived true, following next_cursor through every page, and look for sessions whose created_by_session_id is your session ID and whose title is "Jira <ticket key>". If the listed rows have no archived field, the runner predates include_archived and listed only active sessions, so rely on your earlier replies for archived ones. sys_session_get_info with no arguments returns your session ID and agent ID.

Investigate it and propose a fix.

Watch: new Jira tickets matching this JQL:
project in ("ES", "OPS")

Each run:
1. Read your state from your most recent reply in this session that has a "Checked through:" line: that check time, and any "Delivery pending:" and "Link-back pending:" lines. On the first run, use one hour ago and nothing pending. If you have no way to use Jira here, or signing in to it fails, skip to your reply and say that this automation needs a Jira MCP server where it runs.
2. For each pending delivery, find its session: by its conversation_id, or, for an unconfirmed start listed without one, by its title among the sessions you created (sys_session_list with include_archived true, following next_cursor through every page). If no such session exists and the listed rows carry an archived field (so archived sessions were included), the start never happened: drop the entry, fetch that ticket again by the key in its title, and handle it with this run's matches below, since the search window may have moved past it. If the rows have no archived field, an archived session could be hiding: keep the entry pending and ask the owner in your reply to check for that session. Otherwise read that session's history with sys_session_get_history. If your task message is there, it was delivered: drop the entry. If it isn't, keep the entry pending and point the owner to that session in your reply: the task may still be queued where the history can't show it, so never resend it and never create another session for it.
3. Post each pending link-back, the same way as below. Don't start sessions for them; one that fails again stays pending.
4. Note the current UTC time; it ends this run's window. Then search from 5 minutes before the check time, because new items can take a few minutes to appear. Use your Jira tools to search for (project in ("ES", "OPS")) AND created >= <that time> ORDER BY created ASC. A relative time such as "-90m" avoids time zone mistakes. Leave out results created after the time you noted; the next run picks them up. Read every page of results in that order. If you can't read them all, stop at the last result you read.
5. Skip any ticket you already started a session for, or that is on a "Delivery pending:" line. Check the sessions your earlier replies in this session say you started first. For results not listed there, call sys_session_list once with include_archived true, following next_cursor through every page, and look for sessions whose created_by_session_id is your session ID and whose title is "Jira <ticket key>". If the listed rows have no archived field, the runner predates include_archived and listed only active sessions, so rely on your earlier replies for archived ones. sys_session_get_info with no arguments returns your session ID and agent ID.
6. For each other ticket, oldest first, call sys_session_create with agent_id set to your agent ID, placement "same_host", title "Jira <ticket key>", and a message under 8000 characters.
